note: The stored point is the OpenStreetMap node of Apolianka village itself (48.7361, 30.4043); the Trypillia site lies on the plain near the village (Rassmann et al. 2014, JNA 6), but no readable page prints the site's own point, so no two independent sources can be quoted for it.

The site is the Bronze Age Govurqala by Shahtakhti (Kangarli district), 35 km north-west of Nakhchivan on the left bank of the Araz; only the Wikipedia family (es/ru/az/uk articles, Wikidata) gives its point, 39°22′37″N 45°03′49″E, and no independent source prints coordinates for it. The stored point lies near Vayxır in Babek district, the place of a different Govurqala, about 38 km away, so it is held for the owner.

Pagar Alam is a modern city whose Pasemah megaliths 'surround the town on all sides' (Tegur Wangi, Tanjung Aro, Belumai, Batu Gajah and others); Wikipedia/Wikidata give only the city centre (-4.0167, 103.25), no source gives a point for a single 'Pagar Alam' site or names what lies at the stored point, so no two independent site points can be quoted.

The site is the small Iron Age hillfort, which the Somerset HER (record 10115, 'At the E end of Brean Down', ST 298 588) and the Wikimedia sources (Wikipedia's Somerset hillfort list 51°19′23″N 3°00′37″W; the Atlas of Hillforts point on Wikidata Q4959731, 51°19'27.840"N, 3°0'32.400"W) place at the eastern end of the Down, about 1.3-1.5 km east of the stored point, which is the headland's summit. Only the Wikimedia family gives that point in degrees (the HER gives a grid reference, and the Megalithic Portal misplaces its hillfort entry at the summit), so no two independent sources can be quoted; held for the owner, with the eastern point as the likely correction.

Only Wikipedia (English -6.85, -77.70 and Spanish -6.8506, -77.6931, one source family) prints a point in a readable form; OpenStreetMap maps only the lake, and the one site-specific point found (chachapoya.org, UTM 202400 E 9241756 N, about -6.852, -77.693) is a grid reference, so no two independent quotable sources fix the mausoleums' point.

The stored point equals the Wikidata item Q18210819 (48.5337, 30.3834, carried over from a deleted Wikipedia stub), which falls in Ladyzhynka hromada, Uman Raion, about 10 km west of Perehonivka village (48.5336, 30.5233) where the Ukrainian Wikipedia places a Trypillia settlement; no independent source prints the site's point, so it is held for the owner.

The site is a valley-wide Thracian necropolis of some 1,500 tumuli, not one monument, and the sources place it at unrelated points: Wikidata at 42.6906, 25.3801 (near the stored point), English Wikipedia at the Kazanlak Valley centre 42.58333, 25.54500 (about 18 km away), ancientbulgaria.bg at 42.6218, 25.3986 (Kazanlak town, about 7.7 km away). No two independent sources give the same point, so the point is held for the owner.

The stored point is the centre of the dry Winnemucca Lake bed (Wikipedia/Wikidata of the lake), while the petroglyph site 26Wa3329 lies on the west side of the Winnemucca Lake subbasin; no page prints the site's own point (the Megalithic Portal gives only a rounded 40.14, -119.3 and the Ancient Origins tracker a point 95 km north), so no two independent sources can be quoted for it.

site_name: Bahrain’s Dilmun Burial Mounds - Janabiyah Burial Field
note: The Janabiyah Burial Mound Field (World Heritage component 1542-021) is given a point only by its Wikidata item Q65954052, 26°10'49.080"N, 50°28'23.880"E, 0.08 km from the stored point; the UNESCO component table cannot be read by the checker and no second independent source prints a point for the field (the enwiki/Wikidata point 26.183, 50.466 is the town of Janabiyah), so it is held for the owner.

Only Wikidata (and the Wikipedia-derived mirrors of it) print a point for the Halos; the Historical Marker Database page with its own point refuses the plain GET, and OpenStreetMap has no feature for it, so no second independent source family can be quoted for the point.

The site is the Iron Age trading and workshop settlement on Helgö, which Swedish Wikipedia places on the north-eastern part of the 5 km long island; the stored point is Wikipedia's centre point of the island. The only source giving the settlement's own point, the Megalithic Portal (59.275014N 17.698803E), lies about 1.1 km from the stored point, and no second independent source prints a point for the settlement (the RAA registry needs a script, SightHop hides its point in page code), so the point is held for the owner.

site_name: Cup and Ring marks, Kilmartin Glen
note: The entry is the collective cup-and-ring rock art of Kilmartin Glen, spread over separate panels (Achnabreck about 56.06 N, Cairnbaan 56.063 N, Ballygowan, Baluachraig 56.116 N) up to about 8 km apart. The stored point is Wikipedia's point for the glen as an area (near Kilmartin village, shared with two other entries) and lies at none of the panels; a collective of dispersed panels has no single point that two sources give, so the point is held for the owner.

The excavated Middle Palaeolithic site lies at NHER grid reference TL 8240 9484, which the Megalithic Portal gives as 52.520905N 0.686994E - about 2.5 km north-east of the stored point near Mundford village - but no second independent source prints the site's point in degrees (the Norfolk HER gives only the grid reference, Wikipedia and Wikidata have no coordinates, and the ADS archive and other databases refuse automated requests), so the point is held for the owner.

The stored point equals English Wikipedia's minute-rounded 9°17′S 76°44′W and is about 1.1 km from the site: the Peruvian tourism inventory record (reproduced by Turismo Peruano) gives 9º 16´ 36.4˝ S 76º 43´ 31.6˝ W and Spanish Wikipedia's article on the same site (Cruzpampa) gives -9.276667, -76.725581, but the inventory's coordinate notation cannot be read by the quote checker and no other independent source prints the point, so the correction (about -9.2768, -76.7255) is held for the owner.

Only the English Wikipedia family (and its copies such as Archaeolist) gives the stored point (13.5307 S, 75.3456 W). Wikidata P625 (-13.5433, -75.3794), the OpenStreetMap node of the Complejo Arqueologico de Wiraqocha Pirqa (-13.5399, -75.3779) and the MINCETUR tourism inventory's UTM E 459118 N 8502482 (about -13.5457, -75.3778) all put the site about 3.9 km away, so the stored point is probably wrong, but no second independent source prints that point in a readable coordinate format (the MINCETUR entry is a UTM grid reference, the OSM point is shown by Mapcarta only as separate latitude/longitude lines, and HistoryData/AroundUs copy Wikidata). Held for the owner.
